questions.stem: Listen to the announcement. What is happening?
options: Trains are about twenty minutes late because of rain
Trains are cancelled for the whole day because of snow
Trains are about two hours late because of snow
Trains are about twenty minutes late because of snow
questions.explanation: You heard 「雪のため」 (because of snow) and 「およそ二十分おくれております」 (running about twenty minutes late). 「ため」 after a noun gives the cause, and 「おります」 is the humble form used in announcements.

audio.text: ただいま、雪のため、電車がおよそ二十分おくれております。ごめいわくをおかけして、もうしわけございません。

questions.stem: Listen to the announcement at the station. What should passengers going to Kyoto do?
options: Stay on this train all the way until it reaches Kyoto station
Get off now and wait here for the next train
Buy a new ticket when they reach the next station
Change to the train at the next platform at the next station
questions.explanation: You heard 「次の駅で」 and 「となりのホームの電車にお乗りかえください」. 「乗りかえる」 is to change trains, and 「お…ください」 is the polite request form of announcements.

audio.text: 京都へ行かれる方は、次の駅で、となりのホームの電車にお乗りかえください。

questions.stem: Listen to the announcement in the department store. What is on, and when?
options: A bread sale on the sixth floor from 2 pm
A bread sale on the second floor from 6 pm
A cake sale on the sixth floor from 2 pm
A bread sale on the sixth floor until 2 pm
questions.explanation: You heard 「午後二時から」 (from 2 pm) and 「六かいで」 (on the sixth floor), with 「パンのタイムセール」. 「から」 marks the starting time; 'until' would be 「まで」.

audio.text: ご来店のみなさまにお知らせいたします。本日午後二時から、六かいでパンのタイムセールを行います。

questions.stem: Listen to the school announcement. What are students told?
options: School is closed, and there are no classes at all
School is open, but sport is cancelled because of rain
School is closed, and online classes start at 9 am
School starts late, at 9 am, because of the rain
questions.explanation: You heard 「学校は休みです」 and 「午前九時から、家でオンラインじゅぎょうをうけてください」. 「大雨のよほう」, a forecast of heavy rain, is the reason.

audio.text: 明日は大雨のよほうなので、学校は休みです。午前九時から、家でオンラインじゅぎょうをうけてください。

questions.stem: Listen to the announcement at the museum. What are visitors asked not to do?
options: Take photos, eat or drink inside
Take photos or talk loudly inside
Touch the displays, eat or drink inside
Use their phones or take photos outside
questions.explanation: You heard 「しゃしんをとらないでください」 and 「食べたり飲んだりしないでください」. 「〜ないでください」 asks someone not to do something, and 「たり…たり」 lists examples.

audio.text: この中では、しゃしんをとらないでください。また、食べたり飲んだりしないでください。

questions.stem: Listen to the announcement. What has happened to the fireworks?
options: They have been cancelled completely because of rain
They have been moved to next weekend
They have been moved to 7 pm tomorrow
They will start at 7 pm tonight
questions.explanation: You heard 「雨のため」 and 「明日の夜七時に行うことになりました」. 「〜ことになる」 reports a decision made by others: the event has been moved to tomorrow, not cancelled.

audio.text: 本日の花火大会は、雨のため、明日の夜七時に行うことになりました。

questions.stem: Listen to the announcement at the airport. What should passengers on this flight do?
options: Hurry to Gate 20
Check in at Counter 12
Hurry to Gate 12
Wait at Gate 2
questions.explanation: You heard 「十二番ゲートにおいそぎください」: please hurry to Gate 12. 「ごとうじょうのおきゃくさま」 means the passengers boarding the flight to Melbourne.

audio.text: メルボルン行きにごとうじょうのおきゃくさまは、十二番ゲートにおいそぎください。

questions.stem: Listen to the hotel staff member. What is included in the plan?
options: Neither breakfast nor dinner
Breakfast, but not dinner
Dinner, but not breakfast
Both breakfast and dinner
questions.explanation: You heard 「朝ご飯がついていますが、晩ご飯はついていません」. 「つく」 here means to come with or be included, and 「が」 contrasts the two meals.

audio.text: このプランには、朝ご飯がついていますが、晩ご飯はついていません。

questions.stem: Listen to the phone message. Why is Yuki calling?
options: To say she is running late and will reach the station about 6:30
To say she is early today and will reach the station at about 6:00
To say she has already reached the station at 6:30
To say she cannot come today because the trains are late
questions.explanation: You heard 「おくれそう」 (looks like I'll be late) and 「六時半ぐらいになると思う」. The casual plain style shows she is talking to a friend.

audio.text: もしもし、ゆきです。ごめん、ちょっとおくれそう。駅に着くのは六時半ぐらいになると思う。

questions.stem: Listen to the message from your homestay mother. What does she ask you to do?
options: Buy something for dinner on the way home
Wait for her so you can eat dinner together
Heat up the curry in the fridge for dinner
Cook curry for the family's dinner
questions.explanation: You heard 「れいぞうこのカレーをあたためて食べてね」: heat up the curry in the fridge and eat it. 「仕事で帰りがおそくなるから」 explains that she will be home late.

audio.text: 今日は仕事で帰りがおそくなるから、晩ご飯はれいぞうこのカレーをあたためて食べてね。

questions.stem: Listen to the message. What has changed about the meeting?
options: The place has changed; the time is still ten o'clock
The time has moved from one to ten; the place is the same
The meeting is cancelled and will be held another day
The time has moved from ten to one; the place is the same
questions.explanation: You heard 「十時からではなく、一時からになりました」: not from ten but from one. 「場所は同じです」 confirms that the place has not changed.

audio.text: 明日のミーティングは、十時からではなく、一時からになりました。場所は同じです。

questions.stem: Listen to the message from a classmate. What does Ken want?
options: To see your notes because he was away sick
To lend you his notes because you were away
To ask whether class was cancelled yesterday
To say he has a cold and will miss class tomorrow
questions.explanation: You heard 「ノート、ちょっと見せてもらえない？」, a casual request to see your notes, and 「かぜで休んじゃったんだ」, he was off with a cold. 「休んじゃった」 is the casual form of 「休んでしまった」.

audio.text: けんだけど、きのうのじゅぎょうのノート、ちょっと見せてもらえない？かぜで休んじゃったんだ。

questions.stem: Listen to the message from the shop. What does the customer need to do?
options: Order the book again before Saturday
Wait for the book to be delivered on Saturday
Return the book to the shop on Saturday
Collect the ordered book by Saturday
questions.explanation: You heard 「ごちゅうもんの本が店に入りました」 (the book you ordered has arrived) and 「土曜日までにとりに来てください」. 「までに」 means by a deadline, and 「とりに来る」 is to come and collect.

audio.text: ごちゅうもんの本が店に入りました。土曜日までにとりに来てください。

questions.stem: Listen to the conversation. What do the friends decide to do?
options: Stay home because the beach will be crowded
Go to the beach because the weather is good
See a film because the weather is bad
See a film first and go to the beach later
questions.explanation: One friend suggests a film, the other proposes 「海に行こうよ」 because 「天気がいい」, and the first agrees: 「じゃ、海にしよう」. 「〜にする」 is how a choice is announced.

audio.text: 土曜日、えいがを見に行かない？えいがもいいけど、天気がいいから、海に行こうよ。そうだね。じゃ、海にしよう。

questions.stem: Listen to the conversation between a student and her mother. What do they agree on?
options: She will work on Saturdays instead of Sundays
She will work only on Sundays until her exams finish
She will work on Saturdays and Sundays from now on
She will stop working completely until her exams are over
questions.explanation: The mother objects with 「しけんが近いでしょう」, and the daughter offers a compromise: 「しけんが終わるまでは日曜日だけにする」. 「それならいいよ」 ('in that case, fine') confirms the agreement.

audio.text: お母さん、土曜日もアルバイトをしてもいい？でも、しけんが近いでしょう。じゃ、しけんが終わるまでは日曜日だけにする。それならいいよ。

questions.stem: Listen to the conversation. What do they settle on, and why?
options: Sunday, because the second speaker is busy all day on Saturday
Saturday, because the shops they want are closed on Sunday
Neither day, because the second speaker is too busy to go
Saturday, because the second speaker has family plans on Sunday
questions.explanation: 「日曜日はちょっと…」 is a soft refusal, explained by 「家族と出かけるよていがあるんです」. The first speaker offers Saturday, and 「土曜日ならだいじょうぶです」 accepts it.

audio.text: こんどの日曜日、いっしょに買い物に行きませんか。日曜日はちょっと…。家族と出かけるよていがあるんです。じゃ、土曜日はどうですか。土曜日ならだいじょうぶです。

questions.stem: Listen to the conversation in a shop. What does the customer decide?
options: To buy a different shirt in a larger size
Not to buy the shirt, as there is no larger size
To buy the medium anyway, as it is the only size left
To order a larger size and collect it later
questions.explanation: The assistant says 「エムサイズしかないんです」 (only medium), and the customer replies 「今日はやめておきます」, 'I'll leave it today'. 「しか…ない」 means only, and 「やめておく」 is to decide against something.

audio.text: このシャツ、もう少し大きいのはありますか。もうしわけありません、エムサイズしかないんです。そうですか。じゃ、今日はやめておきます。

questions.stem: Listen to two classmates planning a presentation. How do they share the work?
options: He makes the materials, she does the speaking, and they pick photos together
She makes the materials and speaks, and he picks all the photos alone
They do everything together, including making the materials
She makes the materials, he does the speaking, and they pick photos together
questions.explanation: You heard 「しりょうは私が作るから」 and 「ゆうたくんは話すのをおねがいできる？」, then 「しゃしんはいっしょにえらぼう」. The 「から」 gives her offer as the reason he should take the speaking part.

audio.text: プレゼンのしりょうは私が作るから、ゆうたくんは話すのをおねがいできる？うん、いいよ。じゃ、しゃしんはいっしょにえらぼう。

questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker suggest, and why?
options: Taking the bus, because walking to the station takes thirty minutes
Walking, because the bus to the station takes thirty minutes
Taking the bus, because the bus stop is only three minutes away
Walking, because the bus stop is thirty minutes away
questions.explanation: You heard 「歩くと三十分かかるから」 and 「バスで行ったほうがいい」. 「〜たほうがいい」 gives advice, and 「から」 gives the reason.

audio.text: 駅まで歩くと三十分かかるから、バスで行ったほうがいいと思うよ。

questions.stem: Listen to the interview with an athlete. How did she start?
options: Her father played the sport and taught her when she was small
A teacher at her primary school asked her to join a team
She went to a live match with her father in high school
She watched a match on TV with her father and wanted to try
questions.explanation: You heard 「父といっしょにテレビでしあいを見て」 and 「自分もやってみたいと思ったんです」. 「〜てみたい」 means wanting to try something, and 「んです」 frames it as her explanation.

audio.text: 小学生のとき、父といっしょにテレビでしあいを見て、自分もやってみたいと思ったんです。

questions.stem: Listen to the interview. What is the speaker's attitude to her part-time job?
options: It is hard work, and she wants to quit as soon as she can
It is boring, but the pay makes it worthwhile for her
It is sometimes hard, but she enjoys talking with many people
It is easy, but she finds the customers difficult to deal with
questions.explanation: You heard 「たいへんなこともありますが」 (there are hard times, but) followed by 「いろいろな人と話せるので、とても楽しいです」. The 「が」 turns the sentence towards the positive, which is her overall view.

audio.text: アルバイトはたいへんなこともありますが、いろいろな人と話せるので、とても楽しいです。

questions.stem: Listen to the interview. What does the student want to do in the future, and why?
options: Teach English in Japan, because she likes teaching children
Teach Japanese in Australia, because she likes young people
Study English in Japan, because she wants to travel there
Work with children in Japan, because she likes Japanese food
questions.explanation: You heard 「日本で英語の先生になりたいです」 and the reason, 「子どもにことばを教えるのが好きだから」. 「〜からです」 at the end gives the reason for the sentence before.

audio.text: しょうらいは日本で英語の先生になりたいです。子どもにことばを教えるのが好きだからです。

questions.stem: Listen to the interview with a chef. What does he say matters most?
options: Cooking quickly for customers
Learning from famous chefs
Using food that is in season
Using expensive ingredients
questions.explanation: You heard 「一番たいせつなのは、きせつの食べ物を使うことだ」. 「〜のは…ことだ」 picks out the most important point, and 「きせつ」 means season.

audio.text: りょうりで一番たいせつなのは、きせつの食べ物を使うことだと思います。

questions.stem: Listen to the interview. How long has the speaker lived in Australia?
options: Ten years
Two years
Four years
Twelve years
questions.explanation: You heard 「来てから、もう十年になります」: it has already been ten years since she came. 「もう…になる」 expresses how much time has passed.

audio.text: オーストラリアに来てから、もう十年になります。さいしょは英語がぜんぜんわかりませんでした。

questions.stem: Listen to an older resident. What does he say has changed in his town?
options: The town has grown into a city with many young families
Young people have left for the cities, and there are more elderly people
Young people have moved in from the cities, and there are fewer elderly
Elderly people have moved to the cities to live with their children
questions.explanation: You heard 「わかい人が都会に出ていって」 (young people have gone off to the cities) and 「お年よりがふえました」 (the elderly have increased). This is the ageing society, one of the study design's subtopics.

audio.text: この町は、わかい人が都会に出ていって、お年よりがふえました。

questions.stem: Listen. What is the speaker's opinion of social media?
options: It is useful, but using it too much is bad
It is useless, and nobody should use it
It is harmless, however much you use it
It is useful only for keeping up with news
questions.explanation: You heard 「べんりですが」 (it's convenient, but) and 「使いすぎるのはよくないと思います」. The verb stem plus 「すぎる」 means doing something too much.

audio.text: SNSはべんりですが、使いすぎるのはよくないと思います。

questions.stem: Listen. What is the speaker's attitude to the rule banning phones at school?
options: It does not matter, because nobody at school follows it
It is too strict, though phones should not be used in class
It is fair, and phones should be banned for the whole day
It is too weak, because students still use phones in class
questions.explanation: You heard 「きびしすぎると思う」 (I think it's too strict), but the speaker concedes 「じゅぎょう中は使わないほうがいいのはたしかだ」. A mixed view like this is typical of evaluative answers.

audio.text: 学校でスマホを使ってはいけないというルールは、きびしすぎると思う。でも、じゅぎょう中は使わないほうがいいのはたしかだ。

questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker think people should do for the environment?
options: Buy fewer things when shopping
Walk to the shops instead of driving
Recycle plastic bags after shopping
Take their own bag when shopping
questions.explanation: You heard 「自分のバッグを持っていくべきです」. 「持っていく」 means to take along, and 「べき」 says what people ought to do.

audio.text: かんきょうのために、買い物のときは自分のバッグを持っていくべきです。

questions.stem: Listen. How does the speaker feel about robots caring for elderly people?
options: Robots should replace carers, because they never get tired
Robots are dangerous and should never be used with elderly people
Robots may help, but elderly people need more time talking with people
Robots are the best answer, because there are not enough carers
questions.explanation: You heard 「べんりかもしれませんが」, which grants a point, and 「人と話す時間がもっとひつようだと思います」. The speaker accepts that robots have a use but values human contact more.

audio.text: ロボットはべんりかもしれませんが、お年よりには人と話す時間がもっとひつようだと思います。

questions.stem: Listen. Why does the speaker think studying Japanese is worthwhile?
options: It is easy to learn, and you need it to travel around Japan
It is needed to get into university, and it helps you make friends
It helps you enjoy Japanese films, food and music more
It helps you understand how Japanese people think, and helps your career
questions.explanation: You heard two reasons joined by 「し」: 「考え方がわかるようになる」 and 「しょうらいの仕事にもやくに立ちます」. 「〜ようになる」 describes a change: coming to understand.

audio.text: 日本語を勉強すると、日本の人の考え方がわかるようになるし、しょうらいの仕事にもやくに立ちます。

questions.stem: Listen. What is the speaker's view of online shopping?
options: It is easy, but she misses seeing things in person
It is cheap, but delivery takes too long
It is difficult to use, so she prefers going to real shops
It is fun, and better than shops in every way
questions.explanation: You heard 「楽だけど」 (it's easy, but) and 「店で手にとって見られないのがざんねんだ」, a pity that you cannot pick things up and look at them in a shop. 「見られない」 is the potential negative.

audio.text: ネットで買い物をするのは楽だけど、店で手にとって見られないのがざんねんだ。

questions.stem: Listen. Does the speaker support the plan for a new shopping centre?
options: No, because the area already has too many large shopping centres
No, because old shops would disappear, even though it would be convenient
Yes, because it would be convenient and bring many new shops to the area
Yes, although she is a little worried that some old shops might close
questions.explanation: The speaker grants 「べんりになるのはたしかです」, then 「しかし」 turns to the objection, and 「さんせいできません」 means 'I cannot agree'. 「てしまう」 signals regret at the old shops disappearing.

audio.text: 新しいショッピングセンターができれば、べんりになるのはたしかです。しかし、古い店がなくなってしまうので、私はさんせいできません。

questions.stem: Listen. Where is this conversation most likely taking place?
options: At a train station
In a clothing shop
At a hotel front desk
In a restaurant
questions.explanation: 「何名さまですか」 asks how many are in the party, and showing guests to a seat with a menu places it in a restaurant. A hotel would ask about a booking and a room.

audio.text: いらっしゃいませ。何名さまですか。二人です。では、こちらのおせきへどうぞ。メニューをどうぞ。

questions.stem: Listen. What can you infer about the speaker?
options: She still cannot eat with chopsticks
She is about to leave Japan for good
She is getting used to life in Japan
She has lived in Japan all her life
questions.explanation: You heard 「はしを使うのにもなれて」 (I've got used to chopsticks too) and 「なっとうも食べられるようになりました」 (I can now even eat natto), three months after arriving. These changes show someone adjusting to a new life.

audio.text: 日本に来て三か月、はしを使うのにもなれて、さいきんは、なっとうも食べられるようになりました。

questions.stem: Listen. What is the main topic of the talk?
options: School life in Japan
Technology in Japanese homes
The ageing society in Japan
Tourism in Japan
questions.explanation: You heard 「お年よりのかずがふえて」 (the number of elderly people is rising) and 「働く人のかずがへっています」 (the number of workers is falling). Both point to the ageing society.

audio.text: 日本では、お年よりのかずがふえて、働く人のかずがへっています。

questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker say about the festival?
options: It is held every April, and the townspeople all dance
It is held every August, and visitors watch the dancers
It was held once in August to celebrate the town
It is held every August, and the townspeople all dance
questions.explanation: You heard 「毎年八月に行われて」 (held every August) and 「町の人がみんなでおどります」. 「行われる」 is the passive of 「行う」, to hold an event.

audio.text: このまつりは、毎年八月に行われて、町の人がみんなでおどります。

questions.stem: Listen to the radio advertisement. What is being advertised?
options: A Japanese-learning app, free for the first month
A Japanese school, free for the first year
A new smartphone, sold at half price for one month
A Japanese course held every month at school
questions.explanation: You heard 「スマホで日本語が勉強できる新しいアプリ」 and 「さいしょの一か月はむりょうです」 (the first month is free). Advertisements often add an offer with 「今なら」, 'if you act now'.

audio.text: どこでも、いつでも、スマホで日本語が勉強できる新しいアプリです。今なら、さいしょの一か月はむりょうです。

questions.stem: Listen. Why did the speaker stop driving to work?
options: She now walks to work, to get fit
She now takes the bus, since she moved nearer the station
She now takes the train, to help the environment
She now takes the train, to save money
questions.explanation: You heard 「かんきょうのことを考えて」 (thinking of the environment) and 「電車で行くことにしました」. 「〜ことにする」 reports the speaker's own decision.

audio.text: 前は毎日車で会社に行っていましたが、かんきょうのことを考えて、電車で行くことにしました。

questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker regret?
options: Practising Japanese instead of her other subjects
Not going to Japan while she was in high school
Not practising spoken Japanese more in high school
Choosing to study Japanese at high school at all
questions.explanation: 「〜ばよかった」 expresses regret about something not done: 'I wish I had practised more'. 「ておく」 adds the idea of doing it in advance, to be prepared.

audio.text: 高校のとき、もっと日本語を話すれんしゅうをしておけばよかったと思っています。

questions.stem: Listen to the interview. What does the scientist say robots will do?
options: Be used only in homes and never in workplaces
Help with people's work, though people will still have jobs
Take over all work, so that people will have no jobs left
Stay unhelpful at work for a long time to come
questions.explanation: You heard 「人の仕事を手つだうようになるでしょう」 (will come to help with people's work) and 「人の仕事がなくなることはないと思います」 (I don't think people's jobs will disappear). 「ことはない」 firmly rules something out.

audio.text: これからは、ロボットが人の仕事を手つだうようになるでしょう。でも、人の仕事がなくなることはないと思います。
